facts.fact: Friends of the Boardwalk collected more than 1,000 signatures against concrete.
facts.quote: collected more than 1,000 signatures opposing the use of concrete

facts.fact: By Nov 2014 Parks was about to start a $10 million project with a 10-foot concrete carriage lane; residents sued, lost and appealed.
facts.quote: they lost and filed an appeal.
facts.source_title: CBS New York: Some Brooklyn residents furious over plastic boardwalk

facts.fact: A Parks spokesperson said the new material fits the de Blasio administration's policy of reducing tropical hardwood use.
facts.quote: in line with the de blasio administration's policy of reducing the use of tropical hardwoods

facts.fact: Ida Sanoff described how a concrete-based section of boardwalk already felt harder on the legs for joggers.
facts.quote: you feel it, just as you walk you feel the difference in your legs.

facts.fact: Horseshoe crabs come onto Coney Island Beach every May and June; the highlights page states this directly.
facts.quote: every may and june, horseshoe crabs emerge from the atlantic ocean onto coney island beach.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk Highlights

facts.fact: Crabs prefer to breed at night on high tides within a few days of the full and new moon; one female can lay over 100,000 eggs a season; eggs hatch in 2-4 weeks.
facts.quote: a single female can lay over 100,000 eggs in a single season.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks: Horseshoe Crabs in New York City Parks

facts.fact: Visitor rule: flipping stranded crabs is OK, but never lift them by the tail, which will not grow back if broken; report tagged crabs at fws.gov/crabtag.
facts.quote: it's ok to flip them back - just don't pick them up by the tail!

facts.fact: Crabs are listed as vulnerable by the IUCN, threatened by habitat loss, pollution and harvesting for medical blood testing and bait.
facts.quote: horseshoe crabs are listed as vulnerable by the iucn red list of threatened species

facts.fact: The Parks crab page lists Kaiser Park and Calvert Vaux Park among Brooklyn viewing spots (Coney Island Beach itself is not in that list, though the highlights page says crabs come ashore there).
facts.quote: plumb beach, gerritsen beach, kaiser park, and calvert vaux park in brooklyn

facts.fact: Calvert Vaux Natural Area has a sandy beach along Coney Island Creek designed in 2011 as horseshoe crab spawning habitat; park staff and volunteers monitor crabs yearly.
facts.quote: a sandy beach along coney island creek specifically designed in 2011 to provide horseshoe crab spawning habitat.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks: Calvert Vaux Natural Area

facts.fact: Coney Island Creek Natural Area (Bay View Ave. between Sea Gate Ave. and W. 33 St.) has tidal flats and coastal dunes; migrating birds feed on crab eggs and can double or triple body weight.
facts.quote: can eat enough to double or even triple their body weight before moving on.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks: Coney Island Creek Natural Area

facts.fact: NYC Parks lists Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk as 399.47 acres (park id B169), in Community Boards 13 and 15, ZIPs 11224 and 11235.
facts.quote: acreage: 399.47
facts.source_title: NYC Parks: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk Highlights

facts.fact: A 332-foot cast-concrete wall sculpture by Toshio Sasaki (1946-2007), First Symphony of the Sea, stands on the boardwalk outside the aquarium.
facts.quote: this 332-foot long, ten-foot tall cast-concrete sculpture wall

facts.fact: Coney Island is bounded by West 37th Street and Ocean Parkway, with the Atlantic to the south and Coney Island Creek to the north; once an island, now a peninsula.
facts.quote: once a true island separated by tidal inlets, it is now a peninsula of sand and boardwalks

facts.fact: The Riegelmann Boardwalk, completed in 1923, ran from Sea Gate to Brighton Beach.
facts.quote: the riegelmann boardwalk, completed in 1923, unified the shore from sea gate to brighton beach

facts.fact: The 1970s-90s were hard years of crime, neglect and poverty, yet by the 1990s Coney Island drew millions each summer; the Mermaid Parade began in 1983.
facts.quote: by the 1990s, coney island was once again drawing millions each summer

facts.fact: Oral historian Bobby Nagy remembers 1970s Coney Island as dirty, scary and rough but still alluring.
facts.quote: dirty and scary and rough
facts.source_title: Coney Island History Project: 1970-1979 oral histories

facts.fact: Photographer Lily Binder on the Cyclone: the most cleansing minute of your life because you cannot think.
facts.quote: the cyclone is the most physically and mentally cleansing minute of your life because you can't think.

facts.fact: Peter Agrapides began working in Coney Island in 1949 and owns Williams Candy next to Nathan's.
facts.quote: he began working in coney island in 1949

facts.fact: A Dec 2020 EPA email said the creek would be evaluated further under Superfund after a preliminary assessment found it qualified for an on-site investigation.
facts.quote: coney island creek will be evaluated for further assessment under the comprehensive environmental response, compensation, and liability act
facts.source_title: Brooklyn Paper: Coney Island Creek inches closer to Superfund designation

facts.fact: Ida Sanoff says the creek has dangerously high levels of lead, mercury and pesticides from decades of factory dumping.
facts.quote: has dangerously high levels of lead, mercury, and pesticides

facts.fact: In 2016 the city found 16 Gravesend apartment buildings dumping 200,000 gallons of raw sewage per day into the creek, possibly for years.
facts.quote: 16 apartment buildings in gravesend had been dumping 200,000 gallons of raw sewage into the creek per day

facts.fact: Locals swim, fish and hold religious ceremonies at Kaiser Park on the creek, which environmentalists say risks long-term harm.
facts.quote: many locals use the creek to swim, fish, and conduct religious ceremonies in kaiser park

facts.fact: A Superfund cleanup can take upwards of 20 years.
facts.quote: a process that can take upwards of 20 years

facts.fact: EPA's Dec 2021 site inspection added cyanide and large amounts of the banned ant killer mirex to earlier findings of PCBs, lead and benzene.
facts.quote: added findings of cyanide, significant quantities of a now-banned ant killer called mirex and other toxic compounds
facts.source_title: City Limits: The quest to clean up Coney Island Creek, part 3

facts.fact: As of Nov 2023 the creek was not on the Superfund list: the EPA site manager said the state was reviewing it, and NY DEC does not list water bodies unless they are first federal Superfund sites.
facts.quote: currently, the site is being reviewed by the state programs
facts.source_title: City Limits: Quest to clean up Coney Island Creek, part 3

facts.fact: Coney Island flooded badly from the remnants of Hurricane Ida in early September 2021, and runoff plus sewage flows into the creek from a combined sewer outfall between the Stillwell and Cropsey Avenue bridges.
facts.quote: coney island flooded badly from the remnants of hurricane ida at the beginning of september 2021.

facts.fact: A $15 million bioswale plan for Mermaid Avenue funded after Sandy in 2014 was never built; the high water table was cited.
facts.quote: our water table was too high

facts.fact: NYC sea level has already risen about a foot since 1900, and the 2024 NPCC projects another one to two feet by the 2050s.
facts.quote: the sea levels around new york city have already risen about a foot since 1900

facts.fact: The NPCC projects annual precipitation up to 10% higher by the 2030s and temperatures 2 to 4.7 degrees warmer; Central Park has warmed a quarter degree per decade since 1900.
facts.quote: annual precipitation is expected to increase by up to 10% in those years

facts.fact: The Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice designates Coney Island an environmental justice area.
facts.quote: has earned the neighborhood designation as an environmental justice area

facts.fact: A ferry terminal built for a Kaiser Park pier line was later abandoned; its pilings were removed from the creek.
facts.quote: the since-removed pilings for the abandoned coney island ferry terminal sit in the creek
